reconcile.note: Jamieson, Fausset & Brown read Matthew's fourteen generations as a memory aid, noting Ezra similarly omits six generations of priests between Ezra 7 and 1 Chronicles 6.

discrepancy.note: Strauss shows Matthew's Davidic line omits three kings recorded in 1 Chronicles 3, Ahaziah, Joash, and Amaziah, to force the tally to fourteen.

quotes.text: Firstly, it is said v. 8 Joram begat Ozias ; whereas we know from 1 Chron. iii. 11 , 12 , that Uzziah was not the son, but the grandson of the son of Joram, and that three kings occur between them, namely, Ahaziah, Joash, and Amaziah, after whom comes Uzziah
quotes.attr: David Friedrich Strauss (d. 1874), The Life of Jesus Critically Examined (1846), on Matthew's omission of Ahaziah, Joash, and Amaziah from 1 Chronicles 3.

sides.snippet: and these were born to him in Jerusalem: Shimea, and Shobab, and Nathan, and Solomon, four, of Bathshua the daughter of Ammiel
sides.verseText: and these were born to him in Jerusalem: Shimea, and Shobab, and Nathan, and Solomon, four, of Bathshua the daughter of Ammiel;

sides.snippet: from David to the exile to Babylon fourteen generations
sides.verseText: So all the generations from Abraham to David are fourteen generations; from David to the exile to Babylon fourteen generations; and from the carrying away to Babylon to the Christ, fourteen generations.
